Herbert agreeably surprised us with his running and will be a valuable addition to our "Southern Junior" team. The above and Lucas will form the nucleus of our team, and backed up by such keen and capable performers as Merryman, Powell; Field, Deadman and Selby, they should regain the "Southern Junior" title.
In Clements, Lucas, and the younger Herbert, we have three junior runners destined for the highest rank. Beaumont, Wood and Tobin are all likely to show improved performances next year.

Pack, Michael, Herbert and Bird will value their bronze medals. Our team ran impressively in their heat, and in the final Eddie Pack gave our team a splendid start, unofficial watches timing him to do a shade outside 50 seconds.
Herbert was narrowly beaten in the 880 yards race. When Herbert has learned to run his first 300 yards a little faster and in company, we shall expect him to beat 1 min. 56 sec. for half-mile.
Herbert off with a useful lead. Herbert ran well within himself and kept off the opposition without much trouble.
Herbert off with a slight lead. Roberts, the young Mitcham runner, trailed his man well, but nearing home Herbert went away to win in convincing fashion.
Herbert came with a late burst to win on the tape.
Herbert and Selby were definitely below their usual form, running in 102nd and 113th positions. Johnson, who was in the "B" team, was going very strongly in the 80th position.

However, Beer, Herbert, Edwards, Selby, Shrubb and Boyden should provide a scoring four capable of being placed. The majority of our other juniors are still under nineteen and with the promise they shew may well provide the club with winning teams in years to come.
When they reached the far corner, Smart led Cohen by a yard with Carter and Verney just behind, followed by Arthur Penny, Harry Shields, Jerman, Herbert, Ring, Taylor, Frank Webb and Lucas.
Herbert held the attention of us all. Lucas led the way right from the start, Herbert being content with keeping just behind.

Herbert who, off 50 yards went through the field in fine style and only lost third place in the last few strides. He just failed to overtake Frank Webb, and as the time of the race was 9 min. 30 sec., Herbert must have been doing fast time as he was close up to the leaders at the finish.

Tom Carter shows a gradual return to form, whilst the running of Herbert and Quackenbos, both of whom have done very little training, was very creditable and points to them being very useful team members in the New Year.

Our junior runners have given plenty of evidence of their ability during the present season; and we have every confidence that they will also be prominent in Track events this coming Summer. Herbert's reserve pace gave him a good win, but the form shewn by all our runners inspires confidence in their ability to win the "News of the World" event at the end of the month.

For the 1 Mile we were especially pleased to welcome none other than Len Herbert, our Club Champion, who was home on leave, and he showed that he had lost none of his old form by winning in the very creditable time of 4 min. 35.2 secs.
Herbert, coming down from Staffordshire, arrived too late to start. Dick Towndrow, home on leave from Ireland, finished 5th.

It was Herbert's distinct misfortune to experience a real off-day, not only in the running sense, but physically, too, for as he passed me on every lap he showed unmistakable signs of distress and it must have been sheer "guts" and will-power that enabled him to complete the course.

Len Herbert ran fourth in the 3 Miles, which was won by Gaston Reiff, of Belgium. Willie Nankeville was also selected to represent the A.A.A. in their match at Antwerp, and finished third in the 800 metres event, his time being 1 minute, 58.5 seconds.
Len Herbert, the holder, tried vainly to overtake the leader, but had to be content with second place with John Brown, coming down from Catterick, to gain third position.
There being no Mile race, Len Herbert ran in the 2 Miles event, and after a fine tussle with Tommy Rowe of Herne Hill, Len ran home a good winner in 9 mins. 33.6 secs.

We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson.

Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear.

Owing to sickness there were many notable absentees including both the Herbert's, both the Lucas's and Frank Abberton. The field was led out by Tom Carter but was well together when at 2 miles Carter went into the lead.

Derrick Burfitt was not defending his 1 mile Senior title and Jack Brown ran a good race to beat Len Herbert with Bob Taylor gaining his first club championship medal in third place.

The one mile senior was the race of the afternoon, with a very strong field turning out, but Jack Brown, the holder, ran a well-judged race to come away over the last 200 yards to beat Len Herbert and Chas.

Jack Brown, the holder, was a non-starter, but a small bunch of runners soon detached themselves from the rest of the field with Lucas, Herbert, Tooby, Bromley, Stokell, Bruce and Stearman more or less together.
Len Herbert was on the final relay and he took no chances as Sando of Aylesford, was running the last "leg" for the Paper Mills, who had been having a battle-royal with Essex Beagles.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
The first mile round the top was taken at a reasonable pace but a bunch of about a dozen with Len Herbert on the back of it, soon detached itself from the mob.

Bedford and Walker then made sure of our victory though Charlie took things a little too easy in the middle and so we missed the course record by one second. Burr ran well on the last leg for the "B" team whilst Rolls, Whitehead and Herbert brought the Vets safely home for their prizes.

Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches.
About this time, Bill finished 3rd in the Club Junior 5 miles Championship and scored in a winning Surrey Junior Cross-country team (Wood 1, Herbert 4, Lucas 5, Shepherd 6).
This is the first time we have ever been placed and Messrs. Pack, Michael, Herbert and Bird will value their bronze medals.
